findings.finding: Spec 5.2 S5 lists kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1 among the one-way sysctls and says containment refuses to seal if any value differs; owner decision D3 locks host controls until reboot. The record also accepts 2. In Linux v6.12 only 1 is locked (kernel/bpf/syscall.c bpf_unpriv_handler: locked_state = value == 1; Documentation/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.rst: with 2 'an admin can still change this setting later on'). Probe: a record plus all five captures with unprivilegedBpfDisabled=2 pass check_record, check_capture and check_lifecycle_capture. The README cites spec 5.2 for '1 or 2'; the spec says 1.
findings.location: qualification.schema.json $defs.hardening.unprivilegedBpfDisabled (enum [1,2]); README 'What v2 adds' Host lock state row
findings.requiredChange: Make hardening.unprivilegedBpfDisabled const 1 (keep the observed enum 0..2 so readers can report what they see), correct the README row, and add a record negative (2) and a capture negative (observed 2).

findings.finding: Spec 5.3 requires, for every role, permitted = effective, bounding equal to the listed set and ambient empty. Record and capture carry one 'capabilities' list whose set (effective or permitted) is undefined, so a reader cannot report, and the model cannot refuse, a SERVER whose permitted or bounding set contains CAP_SYS_ADMIN while its effective set is {CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN}; a permitted capability can be raised into effective with capset(2). The README presents the 5.3 capability rows as encoded. Unlike booleans and hardening, the capture cannot express the violating observation.
findings.requiredChange: Keep the enrolled set in the record and make captures report permitted, effective, bounding and ambient separately; refuse unless permitted == effective == bounding == enrolled set and ambient == []; add negatives for an extra permitted capability, an extra bounding capability and a non-empty ambient set.

findings.finding: Spec 4.4 requires refusing a v2 record with a lifecycle subject running inside a resident role cgroup. Only HOST_CONTAINMENT is placed (const cgroupPath; host-wide absence via lifecycleCapture.domainProcessCount). POLICY_WRITER, the subject that may run during ACTIVE (spec 4.1), has no placement field (probe: adding cgroupPath is refused as additionalProperties), and a resident-role capture describes exactly one process, so a POLICY_WRITER process, or any other foreign process, sharing a role cgroup can be neither expressed nor refused. C07 replaces the inspected SERVER process label; it does not model a co-resident process. The record also cannot express that the delegated planeon-capacity-broker.service owns exactly the two leaves broker and probe-worker (spec 4.2), so an extra unenrolled leaf without the seven programs is invisible.
findings.location: qualification.schema.json $defs.lifecycleSubjects.POLICY_WRITER (no placement field) and $defs.capture.process (one process); vectors.json C07
findings.requiredChange: Add a POLICY_WRITER placement rule (a recorded cgroup required to be outside planeon.slice and every role cgroup) and a membership observation in role captures (complete cgroup.procs with a label per member, plus the child list of the delegated broker service); refuse any unenrolled member or child; add record and capture negatives for POLICY_WRITER and HOST_CONTAINMENT inside a role cgroup.

findings.finding: The v2 resource positives differ from the v1 positives only in binding.runNonce and binding.capacityNonce. Their resource manifest is the v1 manifest unchanged (manifestDigest sha256:e455c4a909dc0e47f79d3df287fee5344bf062aac49e050dc4a3668793b13028) and still carries label planeon.ai/run-nonce='unit-nonce' (the v1 run nonce) while binding.runNonce='unit-nonce-v2'; the CREATE name unit-fixture is also the v1 name (C7: signed CREATE names are never reused). The pinned proxy profile contract requires labels == {run-nonce: binding.runNonce, tenant-id: binding.tenantId} (scripts/validate_proxy_contract.py at base 0ecc5f3, lines 167 and 177-178, read only), so the profiles these records pin by profileDigest are invalid and embed v1 nonce data that spec 4.4 says migration never reuses. M01 ('fresh boot and fresh nonces') accepts them because check_record never validates the profile and check_migration compares only scope.runNonce and scope.capacityNonce.
findings.location: vectors.json positive[1] and positive[3] profile.resources[0].manifest; migration M01; native_qualification_v2.py check_record and check_migration
findings.requiredChange: Regenerate positives 1 and 3 with v2 labels (and fresh signed names), recompute manifestDigest, profileDigest, record digests and capture/lifecycle qualificationDigests; state that a valid proxy profile is a precondition of check_record or check it; extend the migration check to every nonce-bearing profile field; add a migration negative for a v2 profile carrying a v1 nonce.

findings.finding: Spec 4.1 requires every backend component to be recorded with its artifact digest, and the model requires its files in the closed inventory, but each file is capped at 64 MiB. Public release metadata (HTTP HEAD content-length, 2026-10-05): kube-apiserver v1.31.0 linux/amd64 90,501,272 B; kube-controller-manager 84,705,432 B; kubelet 76,865,848 B; k3s v1.31.0+k3s1 68,305,048 B; k0s v1.31.1+k0s.0 260,830,864 B (kube-scheduler 63,688,856 B fits). Probe: an APISERVER file of 90,501,272 B is refused at $.files[8].size maximum. The record therefore cannot express the backend of any mainstream distribution checked, an undisclosed W03 selection constraint. The contract also raised files maxItems 128->256 and the inventory bound 512 MiB->1 GiB without disclosure (v1 readiness: 128 files, <=64MiB each, <=512MiB total).
findings.location: qualification.schema.json $defs.file.size (maximum 67108864, unchanged v1 primitive) as applied to backendComponents files; native_qualification_v2.py code inventory bound
findings.requiredChange: Admit realistic control-plane artifacts (a separate backend-file bound if role files must stay at 64 MiB), disclose every bound change relative to the v1 reader bounds, and add a positive with a realistically sized backend file.

findings.finding: The model requires apiIdentity == null exactly for APISERVER, DATASTORE and CONTAINER_RUNTIME. Review finding F1 (carried to W02) and upstream Kubernetes v1.31.0 (staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/config.go AuthorizeClientBearerToken: Name user.APIServerUser = 'system:apiserver', Groups [system:masters]) show the apiserver authenticates its own loopback client, which the rbac/bootstrap-roles hook uses to write policy kinds. The record hard-codes the incomplete closure F1 flagged and makes the required enumeration inexpressible (probe: APISERVER apiIdentity 'system:apiserver' refused 'backend API identity'). Spec 2.3 and 4.1, which the README cites, do not support the null rule.
findings.location: native_qualification_v2.py NO_API_IDENTITY and check_record 'backend API identity'; README Backend components row; vectors.json R21
findings.requiredChange: Let the APISERVER entry carry its in-process identities (string or list) and leave exact values to W02g; remove the null-for-APISERVER rule and correct the README attribution; keep null only where no API client exists (DATASTORE, CONTAINER_RUNTIME).

findings.finding: Spec P1 (datastore socket connectto from the apiserver domain alone), P4 (signing key readable only by the apiserver and controller-manager domains), P9 (runtime socket only from the kubelet domain) and 2.3 (each identity in its own domain) presume distinct per-component domains, and 5.3 forbids unconfined domains anywhere. The model only refuses planeon_* labels and paths under planeon.slice. Probes ACCEPTED: all six components in kube_apiserver_t; APISERVER in unconfined_t, init_t, kernel_t or spc_t; KUBELET cgroupPath '/opt/not-a-cgroup' or the root '/sys/fs/cgroup'; every component in one cgroup; SCHEDULER sharing the KUBELET node identity. Decision 4 (shared executables) as encoded thus admits a single-process, single-domain control plane that cannot meet P1/P4/P9. No capture variant observes backend processes, so recorded labels and cgroups are never compared with an observation.
findings.location: native_qualification_v2.py check_record backend loop; qualification.schema.json $defs.backendComponent; README decision 4
findings.requiredChange: Require pairwise-distinct processLabel and cgroupPath (under /sys/fs/cgroup, not the root) and distinct apiIdentity values across backend components; refuse known unconfined or privileged types or bind labels to the W02e matrix; restate decision 4 as 'a shared file is allowed only with separate processes in separate domains'; add a backend capture or name the observation that checks these fields; add negatives.

findings.finding: All 42 negatives replay to exactly their stated refusal, but coverage has gaps: no vector for a backend component sharing a role artifact (the rule 'backend code shared with a planeon role' is never exercised), for a resident role loading lifecycle code (R31 tests the inverse direction), for HOST_CONTAINMENT cgroupPath inside a role cgroup (spec 4.4), for the internal-tuple collision rule (reachable only through a signed tuple equal to the I06 tuple; R28 is refused earlier by the schema enum), for gate outbound, server endpoints or broker/worker grants, for the gate CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE coupling in either direction, for capacityNonce reuse, for record-level planeon_containment_enabled, modulesDisabled, kexecLoadDisabled or unprivilegedBpfDisabled, non-empty mapIds, intra-role program sharing, the gate under the BROKER key, or lifecycle-capture binding, expiry and seal path. The ten crossVersion entries use four IDs (X01 x4, X02 x4), record no expected refusal, are refused on structural errors ('schema $ required') rather than the version discriminator, and X03/X04 cover one positive each; the v1-reader path-only case is not vectored (probe: refused at $.roles.SERVER.cgroup.path const). M03 carries a stray 'kind' key. C07's intent ('containment-domain process inside a resident role cgroup') overstates what it tests.
findings.location: vectors.json negative, crossVersion and migration arrays
findings.requiredChange: Add the missing negatives with exact refusals, give crossVersion entries unique IDs and expected refusals, add path-only cross-version vectors for both readers and for captures, and align C07's intent with what it tests.

findings.finding: Code ownership is compared by path only. Probes ACCEPTED: OBSERVER loading a byte-identical copy (same sha256 and verityDigest) of the HOST_CONTAINMENT executable at another path; KUBELET's executable byte-identical to the EFFECT_GATE artifact at another path. The README rules 'their code may not be loaded by a resident role' and 'never with a planeon role or lifecycle subject' are bypassed by a copy.
findings.location: native_qualification_v2.py check_record 'used' ownership map; README decision 4 and Lifecycle subjects row
findings.requiredChange: Compare sha256 and verityDigest across owner classes (role, each lifecycle subject, backend) in addition to paths, and add negatives for content-identical copies.

findings.finding: These functions only schema-validate the record; none runs check_record. Probe: with SCHEDULER in planeon_server_t, check_record refuses, but all five captures, the lifecycle capture and check_migration accept. The README defines no acceptance rule saying a v2 qualification needs check_record plus captures for all five roles plus the lifecycle capture, in one boot and window.
findings.requiredChange: Either call check_record inside each check (passing profile and endpoints) or define and vector an aggregate acceptance function, and document that the individual checks are not acceptance on their own.

findings.finding: Predecessors are not validated against the pinned v1 schema; only schemaVersion is read. Probes ACCEPTED: predecessor {bootId: null, runNonce: null, capacityNonce: null}; a predecessor carrying the v2 boot ID in upper case (the v1 schema requires lower case); a v2 runNonce equal to the v1 capacityNonce (cross-field reuse). No vector covers capacityNonce reuse.
findings.requiredChange: Validate each predecessor against the pinned v1 schema (sha256 bef248bfa82b234124c014f98e40c5791bced3171bb118b7ed1bb7b8daaf95c3), compare every v2 nonce against every v1 nonce, and add vectors.

findings.finding: Aliasing is refused only through distinct const strings. Probes ACCEPTED: the gate listener (KUBERNETES_API_PROXY) and the SERVER listener (CAMPAIGN_PROXY) as two signed IDs with one tuple 127.0.0.1:9443; EFFECT_GATE and SERVER cgroups with the same inode.

findings.finding: The closed schema has no field that binds several spec 5.1-5.3 items, so each needs a new record version later: RLIMIT_CORE=0; seccomp default action KILL_PROCESS and the per-role, per-architecture filter (W02d) (only seccompMode const 2 is recorded, and inspection.bpfCommands is a constant tied to no filter); the S5 loaded kernel module set ('exact list is W02 data', not listed as deferred); labels of the planeon cgroup directories and pin/program ownership, which review finding F2 identifies as the real control.
findings.requiredChange: Add binding slots now (e.g. per-role seccompFilterDigest per machine, rlimitCore, cgroup selinuxLabel, pin label and owner, moduleSetDigest) or state which later version or W02 part adds each and that v2 alone does not bind them.

findings.finding: Decisions that are not listed as decisions, or are attributed to spec text that does not state them: (a) HOST_CONTAINMENT placed in planeon.slice (spec 4.2 lists only the resident services; S2 only names the unit); (b) EFFECT_GATE interpreterPath const null (native-only gate; spec silent); (c) the lifecycle code-sharing rule is attributed to spec 4.1/5.2, which do not state it; (d) the internal I06 endpoint is the first outbound tuple not in the signed envelope, departing from NATIVE_QUALIFICATION_READINESS ('Per-role tuples are an explicit subset of the existing envelope/capacity, not a new endpoint authorization') without saying what authorizes its port, and decision 2's stated purpose (comparison with enrolled BPF tuples) is not realizable because the record carries no tuple content; (e) the inventory bound changes in F5.
findings.location: README 'What v2 adds' and 'Decisions made in this contract'; qualification.schema.json
findings.requiredChange: List each as a decision with rationale, state the authorization source of the internal tuple (e.g. sealed apiserver configuration or the planeon_kubeapi_port_t label from W02e), and correct the spec attributions.

findings.finding: Spec 4.1: backendComponents keys are fixed by the selected implementation profile version and missing keys refuse. Nothing binds a key set to backendProfile.implementationId; the positives use the same implementationId 'unit-distribution' with six keys in zero-resource mode and eight in resource mode, contrary to P10 (same backend view in both modes) and the 'no mode-dependent branch' rule. questionAnswers.Q1: Partly. Encoded as consts or checks: record/profile versions; all five resident roles required with exact executables, labels, uids, cgroups, seccomp mode 2 and no_new_privs 1; closed lifecycle subjects with digest, domain and entry; closed backend keys; gate identity, listener (the KUBERNETES_API_PROXY endpoint when resources exist) and outbound (internal loopback only); reader commands {7,15,16}; pin layout; BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI, helper-free, map-free programs; bpf_jit_harden 0/1; the three booleans; lockdown=integrity, modules_disabled=1, kexec_load_disabled=1, ptrace_scope=3; seal marker; capability consts and the CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE coupling. Weakened: unprivileged_bpf_disabled accepts 2 (F1); capability set relations (F2); spec 4.4 placement of POLICY_WRITER and role-cgroup membership (F3); backend per-component separation and unconfined domains (F7); missing optional backend keys (F15). Not expressible: upstream backend binaries over 64 MiB (F5), the apiserver loopback identity F1 requires (F6), per-controller identities (F19), RLIMIT_CORE, seccomp default action and filter binding, module set, cgroup/pin labels (F13). Added without spec support: APISERVER null API identity (F6), HOST_CONTAINMENT in planeon.slice, native-only gate, raised inventory bounds, the lifecycle code rule's attribution, the unsigned internal tuple (F14). Decisions: 1 acceptable, but marker content and tmpfs are unverified (F17); 2 consistent with P2, but a departure from the v1 signed-envelope rule with unstated authorization (F14); 3 acceptable and consistent with S3 (cross-role sharing vectored by R26, intra-role not); 4 as encoded permits collapsing domains, cgroups and identities and is checked by path only (F7, F9).
questionAnswers.Q2: The paths are exact and consistent with spec 4.2: SERVER /sys/fs/cgroup/planeon.slice/planeon-proxy-server.service, OBSERVER .../planeon-policy-observer.service, EFFECT_GATE .../planeon-effect-gate.service, BROKER .../planeon-capacity-broker.service/broker, WORKER .../planeon-capacity-broker.service/probe-worker, all schema consts; HOST_CONTAINMENT .../planeon-host-containment.service goes beyond 4.2 (F14). v1/v2 mutual rejection holds for records (v2 consts; R07; X01 x4 refused; the v1 schema pins planeon-live/*, so X02 x4 are refused and a v1 record changed only in the SERVER path is refused at $.roles.SERVER.cgroup.path const) and for captures (X03 refused under v2, X04 refused under the v1 schema; a v2 BROKER capture observing the v1 path is refused 'process/kernel custody differs'). The cross-version refusals are structural rather than path-isolated, and only R07 isolates a path (F8). F3 is closed. The v1 direction was checked against the v1 schema only; the v1 validator was not run.
questionAnswers.Q3: 42/42 negatives replay to exactly their stated refusal, and none fails on an incidental rule, though C07's intent overstates its test. Spec 4.4 cases covered: v1 under v2 (X01, R01), v2 under v1 (X02), missing EFFECT_GATE (R02), extra role (R03), gate at the broker executable/path/domain (R04-R06), unknown backend key (R17), migration boot/nonce (M02, M03). 'Gate under the BROKER key' is not directly vectored (schema consts refuse it). 'Lifecycle subject inside a resident role cgroup' has only C07 and cannot be expressed for POLICY_WRITER (F3). Duplicated pins are prevented by the exact layout rule (R25). Important refusals without a vector are listed in F8, notably a backend sharing a role artifact (rule never exercised; probes show it fires by path, while copies bypass it, F9) and a resident role loading lifecycle code (only the inverse, R31). Cross-version entries have duplicate IDs and no expected refusals (F8).
questionAnswers.Q4: Yes. The model wrongly accepts: unprivileged_bpf_disabled=2 in record and captures (F1); captures whose single capability list hides permitted, bounding or ambient differences (F2, by construction); co-resident foreign or POLICY_WRITER processes (F3, by construction); positives that reuse v1 nonce data (F4); all backend components in one domain or cgroup, unconfined/init/kernel/spc domains, non-cgroupfs paths and shared identities (F7); byte-identical copies of lifecycle or gate code (F9); captures, lifecycle capture and migration against a record that check_record refuses (F10); unvalidated or cross-field-reusing migration predecessors (F11); aliased listener tuples and duplicate cgroup inodes (F12); missing optional backend keys (F15). Ordering: every check validates the schema before semantics, but check_capture, check_lifecycle_capture and check_migration never run check_record. Endpoint/capability coupling is correct for SERVER and EFFECT_GATE in both directions (R22; probes with gate port 443 with and without the capability). Code ownership is path-based. Capture equality is exact for the inspected process, files, maps, programs, pins and host lock state, but it is order-sensitive for capabilities (false refusal, F18) and cannot see other cgroup members.
